transcript: last night my friend Jonathan and I saw Pal Joey at New York City Center. Pal Joey is a 1940s musical about an ambitious man named Joey who's trying to make it as musician while navigating love and temptations — tale as old as time, right? Although technically a revival, this production featured a completely new book which notably framed Joey as a black man struggling to make a name for himself among the wealthy white population while maintaining true to his identity and his artistry. This definitely added an interesting layer to the story but overall Joey was still a little hard to root for — he still seemed kind of sleazy and directionless. If the story was lacking though, the performances certainly made up for it. The incredible band was featured heavily throughout the show and all of the actors were phenomenal too — Aisha Jackson as Linda English was a standout. I find that with City Center productions you sometimes leave thinking, “I can see why this show is seldom produced” but you never leave dissatisfied with the performances. Overall Pal Joey was far from perfect but still quite enjoyable. With that, another playbill for my collection
